text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today to $137.20, continuing a sharp five-day rally that has lifted the stock nearly 5% since late August. The climb tracks directly with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East: Iran struck Kuwait with missiles and drones on September 3rd, following earlier U.S. strikes against Iranian targets and Iranian retaliatory attacks on U.S. Gulf allies. These hostilities have pushed global oil prices higher — Brent crude moved above $95 a barrel — raising the value of crude that refiners and producers like ConocoPhillips can extract and sell.

The risk of disruption to oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's critical chokepoints, amplifies the supply-worry premium. With over 17 million barrels transiting the strait daily and tensions spiking, investors are pricing in tighter global oil supply and higher prices ahead, which directly benefits an integrated energy producer's margins and cash flow.
